hens_rule_text: Up to 5 hens with a city Backyard Hen permit on single-family lots up to 1 acre; up to 10 on 1 to 2 acres and 15 on lots over 2 acres (city permit page). Agriculture and Rural Residential-Acre zones keep their own broader rights.
permit_notes: Backyard Hen Program permit ($25) under Ordinance 2015-0337-E. Apply with the city form, a UF/IFAS Extension chicken-keeping seminar certificate and a sketch of the property showing the coop.
setback_notes: Coops must meet accessory-structure setbacks in Sec. 656.403 (reported as 5 ft from side and rear lot lines) and sit in the back yard; not allowed in front or side yards except corner and through lots.
coop_rules: Hens kept in a covered, ventilated, predator-secure coop or enclosure at all times, screened from neighbors by an opaque fence or barrier, at least 3 sq ft per bird, max 6 ft tall; coops over 100 sq ft need a building permit; feed in rodent-proof containers.
zoning_notes: Allowed by permit only on single-family lots. Prohibited on duplex, triplex and multi-family properties, and in mobile home parks, RV parks and rental communities. No selling of chickens, eggs or manure from the property.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Jacksonville, Backyard Hen Program Permit (Current Planning)
Jacksonville Ordinance Code Sec. 656.422, Chickens allowed by permit in certain zoning districts

research_notes: Read the city's Backyard Hen Program permit PDF via an Internet Archive copy (live URL now 404s); it states hen tiers, the rooster ban and permit steps. Slaughter ban and the 5 ft accessory setback come from search extracts of Sec. 656.422, which could not be opened; one extract describes the large-lot allowance as 5 more hens per extra half acre, which differs from the city page tiers.
